x: Cytokinins are plant hormones that promote cell division and delay ageing. Insulin, thyroxin and oestrogen are animal hormones. (Off-topic: plant physiology.)
source: PMF General Science Part 4 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-04.txt) p.1

x: The gene is the basic physical and functional unit of heredity. Chromosomes and DNA carry genes, and the nucleus houses them, but the unit of heredity is the gene.
source: PMF General Science Part 3 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-03.txt) p.27-31; NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.64

x: A transgenic organism carries a gene from a different species inserted artificially into its genome, as in Bt cotton. It is not just any natural or extreme-climate organism, nor only bacteria.
source: NextGen Environment APPSC 12 (src/environment/nextgen-environment-appsc-12.txt) p.9 ("A transgenic plant contains a gene or genes of a different species"); NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.71

x: DNA has adenine, guanine, cytosine and thymine. Uracil replaces thymine in RNA, so it is not a component of DNA.
source: PMF General Science Part 3 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-03.txt) p.27, p.31

x: Behaviour therapy applies the principles of learning theory (conditioning) to change behaviour. Play therapy, eclectic therapy and shock therapy are not based on learning theory. (Off-topic: psychology.)
source: general knowledge, not checked

x: Ribozymes are RNA molecules with catalytic (enzyme) activity. They are not DNA, and they are not inactive.
source: PMF General Science Part 3 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-03.txt) p.9 ("Some RNA molecules, called ribozymes, have catalytic activity"), p.22

x: Functional chromosomes cannot yet be built by joining DNA segments from cells of different species, so (a) is the wrong statement. Artificial functional DNA, DNA replication outside a cell (PCR) and cell division in petri dishes (tissue culture) are all achieved.
source: PMF S&T Part 2 (src/science-tech/pmf-science-tech-02.txt) p.91 (PCR); PMF S&T Part 3 (src/science-tech/pmf-science-tech-03.txt) p.1-2 (tissue culture); UPSC 2019 key (a), printed key

x: Gene therapy treats a hereditary disease by correcting the faulty gene. A normal gene is delivered to replace or compensate for the defective one, so "treating the diseased genes" is the printed key. Radium treatment and chemotherapy are not gene therapy.
source: OnlyIAS NCERT S&T Part 12 (src/science-tech/onlyias-ncert-science-tech-12.txt) p.21 (gene therapy = correction of a gene defect by delivering a normal gene); PMF S&T Part 3 (src/science-tech/pmf-science-tech-03.txt) p.47
dispute: Printed key: treating the diseased genes. Most textbooks word it as replacement of defective genes with normal ones (OnlyIAS NCERT S&T Part 12 p.21). Both describe the same method.

x: "Eve" was the name Clonaid gave in December 2002 to the baby girl it claimed was the first human clone. The claim was never verified. Dolly was the cloned sheep (1996).
source: general knowledge, not checked; NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.3 (Dolly the sheep)

x: Genome mapping means mapping genes, that is, finding the relative positions of genes and DNA sequences on chromosomes. It has nothing to do with blood groups, nerve centres or the brain.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.64 (genome, sequencing); PMF S&T Part 2 (src/science-tech/pmf-science-tech-02.txt) p.92

x: Genetic engineering has achieved disease resistance, growth promotion and animal cloning (Dolly). Human cloning has had no fruitful result and is banned, so the answer is 1, 2 and 3.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.3-4 (Dolly, first cloned mammal); PMF S&T Part 3 (src/science-tech/pmf-science-tech-03.txt) p.28-29 (cloning, GE in livestock)

x: Biochips are DNA-, RNA- and protein-based chips used in genetic diagnostics, drug discovery and basic research.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.61 ("DNA/RNA/protein-based biochips used in basic research")

x: Putting a human growth-hormone gene into a mouse moves a gene from one species to another, which is genetic engineering. It is not hybridisation, mutation breeding or hormonal feeding.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.71 (GMO = gene from one organism to another)

x: rDNA technology moves genes between unrelated species: plant to plant, animal to plant and microbe to higher organism. All three statements are correct.
source: PMF S&T Part 2 (src/science-tech/pmf-science-tech-02.txt) p.90-91 (UPSC 2013, answer 1, 2 and 3); NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.62 ("rDNA → Higher organism")

x: Gene maps help trace livestock pedigree and breed disease-resistant animals, so I and III are correct. II overstates: gene positions do not reveal the causes of all human diseases.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.64; UPSC 2011 key (c), printed key

x: GE plants have been made for drought tolerance, higher nutritive value (golden rice) and longer shelf life (Flavr Savr tomato). Photosynthesis in spaceships is not an established GE goal, so most keys give 1, 2 and 4.
source: PMF S&T Part 3 (src/science-tech/pmf-science-tech-03.txt) p.7-8; NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.3 (Flavr Savr); https://superkalam.com UPSC 2012 S&T (web search: 1, 2 and 4)
evidence: PMF S&T Part 3 (src/science-tech/pmf-science-tech-03.txt) p.8 (answer all four)
web search: superkalam / examrobot UPSC 2012 (1, 2 and 4)
dispute: Most keys and books: 1, 2 and 4. PMF S&T Part 3 p.8 marks all four (it counts space agriculture research).

x: Tears contain lysozyme, an antibacterial enzyme that breaks down bacterial cell walls. Ptyalin is in saliva, pepsin in the stomach, and sebum is skin oil. (Off-topic: human physiology.)
source: general knowledge, not checked; PMF General Science Part 2 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-02.txt) p.41 (lysozyme in saliva)

x: DNA ligase seals the Okazaki fragments of the lagging strand into a continuous strand. Helicase unwinds DNA, polymerase adds nucleotides, and reverse transcriptase copies RNA into DNA.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.68 (DNA ligase joins DNA fragments); Okazaki detail: general knowledge, not checked

x: Agrobacterium tumefaciens causes crown gall disease. Its Ti plasmid makes it the main tool for plant genetic engineering, and so it is useful to modern agriculture. All three are true.

x: The origin of replication (ori) is the specific DNA sequence where replication starts. DNA linked to it can multiply in the host.
source: OnlyIAS NCERT S&T Part 12 (src/science-tech/onlyias-ncert-science-tech-12.txt) p.14, p.16 ("origin of replication, which is responsible for initiating replication")

x: Adenoviruses have double-stranded DNA genomes and retroviruses have single-stranded RNA, so statement 1 reverses them. Some colds are caused by adenoviruses and AIDS by the retrovirus HIV, so only 2 is correct.
source: PMF S&T Part 3 (src/science-tech/pmf-science-tech-03.txt) p.47 (adenovirus, retrovirus as vectors); UPSC 2021 key (b); genome types: general knowledge, not checked

x: A virus contains only one kind of nucleic acid, either DNA or RNA. Amoeba, bacteria and plant cells have both.
source: general knowledge, not checked; PMF General Science Part 3 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-03.txt) p.27-31 (DNA and RNA)
evidence: no printed key (k:u); keyed from general knowledge

x: PCR copies a chosen DNA segment in a thermocycler using heat-stable Taq polymerase, in a tube and without any living cells. Every printed option speaks of living or dead cells, so none is correct (printed key: DNA using living cells).
source: PMF S&T Part 2 (src/science-tech/pmf-science-tech-02.txt) p.91 (PCR steps 94-98 °C, Taq polymerase); https://www.genome.gov/about-genomics/fact-sheets/Polymerase-Chain-Reaction-Fact-Sheet
evidence: genome.gov PCR fact sheet (thermocycler machine reaction)
web search: PCR is done in a test tube, not in living cells

x: Restriction endonucleases are called molecular scissors because they cut DNA at specific sites. Ligase joins DNA, polymerase builds it, and reverse transcriptase copies RNA into DNA.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.67 ("Popular description: Molecular scissors")

x: Plasmids are small circular extra-chromosomal DNA molecules of bacteria. They are the commonest vectors in genetic engineering. Plastids, mitochondria and ribosomes are not vectors.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.68 (plasmid = vector)

x: Escherichia coli (host for cloning) and Agrobacterium tumefaciens (Ti-plasmid vector for plants) are the two bacteria most used in genetic engineering.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.69 (E. coli vector pBR322); PMF S&T Part 3 (src/science-tech/pmf-science-tech-03.txt) p.6 (Agrobacterium-mediated transformation)

x: Agrobacterium tumefaciens causes crown gall disease through its Ti plasmid. Bacillus thuringiensis is an insect pathogen and Pseudomonas fluorescens a biocontrol agent.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.40 (Agrobacterium tumefaciens – crown gall)

x: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific base sequences (recognition sites). Joining fragments is the job of DNA ligase, the tempting wrong option.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.67; PMF S&T Part 2 (src/science-tech/pmf-science-tech-02.txt) p.86

x: Restriction endonucleases are the chemical scissors that cut DNA at specific sites. Ligase is the glue that joins fragments, and a plasmid is a vector.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.67; PMF S&T Part 2 (src/science-tech/pmf-science-tech-02.txt) p.86 ("DNA Scissors (Restriction Enzymes)")

x: Blockchain belongs with digital currency. The Belle II experiment is particle physics, not AI, and CRISPR-Cas9 is gene editing, not particle physics. So only B is matched.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.66 (CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing); UPSC 2018 key (b)

x: Insulin was the first human hormone made by rDNA technology: Humulin, approved in 1982. Estrogen, testosterone and thyroxine were not.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.3 ("First human hormone produced by recombinant-DNA technology: Insulin")
